A group of 35 amazing corporate women professionals came together to paint, unwind, and embrace creativity. I began the session with a little introduction about Van Gogh, sharing what inspires me about his art and why I chose this masterpiece for the day. From the very first brushstroke, the energy in the room was electric—smiles, laughter, and pure joy filled the space. Their excitement, compliments, and words of appreciation truly made my day! 

By the end of the session, everyone said the same thing: *”We need more of this in our busy office lives!”* Hearing that reaffirmed everything I believe in—art has the power to heal, inspire, and bring people together.

Yesterday was a reminder of how far I’ve come, how fulfilling this journey is, and how proud I am to be doing what I love.

Reason why people choose preserving memories through resin art??? Wanted to clarify few points as well..

We’ve received a range of feedback on preserving cherished memories through resin art, both positive and negative. Some people feel it may be excessive to preserve precious items in this way, suggesting that these items could be given to those in need or that they may be lost to future generations because they can no longer be touched or appreciated in their original form. While we understand these perspectives, it’s important to recognize the deep emotional significance behind why someone might choose to preserve their memories in this manner.

Many people have shared that, over the years, they’ve kept their precious items in a drawer or cabinet, often forgetting about them until a move or shift in life prompts them to rediscover them. Unfortunately, some of these items have been lost or damaged due to time, neglect, or environmental factors like insects. The idea of permanently preserving these keepsakes offers peace of mind and ensures that they won’t be lost again, creating a tangible connection to the past. For many, it’s not just about the items themselves, but the emotions and memories attached to them—things that words can’t fully capture.

Before we judge or dismiss someone’s decision, it’s important to consider the deeply personal, meaningful reasons behind their choices. For some, this form of art is a way to preserve a lifetime of memories and emotions in a way that gives them comfort and assurance for years to come.

caption:
From Trash to Masterpiece❤️

When we rented our studio, I discovered two large canvases left behind by the previous tenants. They were covered in trash, but seeing these big canvases filled me with a sudden joy. I couldn’t bear to let them go to waste, so I brought them into the studio and kept them safe. At that moment, I had no idea what I was going to do with such large canvases, as I had never worked on anything so big in my life. The canvases were already painted in a sky-blue color with a mild texture, and I hung them on the wall.

One day, a friend visited the studio and commented, This canvas looks so empty. I think it’s waiting for something special to fill it. That simple observation sparked something inside me.

One night, the idea struck me—an idea inspired by Van Gogh’s Starry Night, but with a twist. I envisioned creating a textured version of the painting, unlike anything I had seen before. I set to work, using over 3,000 brushstrokes to build up the texture, layer by layer. Every stroke was an expression—of healing, joy, the thrill of holding the brush, the colors of my life, and the language of love. It took me 48 hours to complete the piece, but when it was done, I felt it was more than just a painting—it was a journey of self-expression.

We displayed the painting in our art street, and people started calling it a “masterpiece.”
